author: Grand Canyon Times
title: Arizona bill secures Chase Field's future without new taxes
text:
Jeff Weninger, Arizona State Representative for 13th District | www.azleg.gov
Jeff Weninger, Arizona State Representative for 13th District | www.azleg.gov
Legislation aimed at securing the future of Chase Field and keeping the Arizona Diamondbacks in Phoenix is expected to be signed into law soon. The bill, HB2704, sponsored by State Representative Jeff Weninger, has received bipartisan support and favorable comments from Governor Hobbs.
HB2704 proposes a funding mechanism for repairs and upgrades at Chase Field without increasing taxes. It allows existing sales and income tax revenues generated by the team and its events to be redirected towards the stadium's maintenance. The Arizona Diamondbacks have pledged at least $250 million for future repairs and renovations, adding to over $200 million already invested.
Representative Weninger said, "This is a smart, responsible solution that keeps the Diamondbacks where they belong—at Chase Field in the heart of our capital city." He emphasized that costs would be covered by revenue from team activities rather than new taxes.
With the team's lease expiring in 2027, HB2704 addresses calls for a long-term solution to keep the team in Arizona. Derrick Hall, President and CEO of the Arizona Diamondbacks, expressed gratitude for the leadership shown with HB2704. "The voting results and bipartisan enthusiasm clearly showed the need for funding for this economically generating public asset," he said.
Chase Field has hosted over 55 million fans since its opening in 1998. The new legislation aims to ensure it remains a top venue without additional state funds or tax burdens on Arizona families.
